outcomes.text: Use the definite and indefinite article forms.
Recognise and form nouns of all standard and common irregular types.
Recognise and form adjectives of all standard and common irregular types.
Form adverbs and compare adjectives and adverbs.
Recognise pronouns, pronominal adjectives and related forms.
Use cardinal numbers 1 to 1000 and ordinal numbers 1st to 10th.
Use prepositions with their cases.
Recognise and form standard, common irregular, impersonal and defective verbs from both conjugations in all moods, voices and tenses.
Form compound verbs of regular formation with common prefixes, including consonant and vowel changes.
Use the standard patterns of case usage.
Use negation, including compound negatives.
Use direct statement, question (including deliberative) and command.
Use prohibitions, exhortations and wishes.
Use the infinitive as subject, complement, prolative and with the definite article.
Use the participle, including the genitive absolute.
Express comparison, including the genitive of comparison.
Use verbal nouns and adjectives.
Use the particle ἄν.
Use indirect statement (including extended reported speech), question, command and prohibition.
Use descriptive relative clauses and participial constructions.
Use subordinate clauses within indirect speech.
Use purpose clauses.
Use result clauses.
Use conditional clauses.
Use causal clauses.
Use temporal clauses.
Use indefinite clauses.
Use clauses of fearing, prevention and precaution.
Use concessive and comparative clauses.
Recognise, analyse and use the accidence and syntax listed for the language components.
Extend vocabulary and linguistic structures through wider reading of Classical Greek.
Translate unseen narrative prose (Xenophon) into English accurately.
Translate unseen verse (Euripides, iambic trimeter) into English accurately.
Scan lines of unseen verse.
Distinguish words of identical spelling but different accentuation.
Translate unseen English into Classical Greek, writing breathing marks.
Show understanding of an unseen oratory passage through comprehension, translation and syntax and accidence questions.
Show detailed understanding of the linguistic structures of ancient authors, from individual words to sentences.
Show detailed knowledge and understanding of the prose set texts studied in Greek.
Read selected ancient literature in English translation to understand the literary context of the set texts.
Understand the social, cultural and historical contexts of the texts, their authors and audiences.
Identify, analyse and evaluate literary techniques, characterisation, argument and meaning using technical terms.
Translate passages of a set text into English.
Write at length, selecting evidence from the set text and translated material.
Study Herodotus Book 7 (Thermopylae) and Book 8 (Artemisium) set passages, with related English passages.
Study Plato's Crito, 43a to the end, with the English sections.
Study the set passages of Lucian's Charon, with the rest in English.
Study Herodotus Book 3 set passages, with English sections.
Study Plato's Laches set passages, with the English sections.
Study Demosthenes' Third Philippic, 1-33, with the rest in English.
Show detailed knowledge and understanding of the verse set texts studied in Greek, including metre.
Read selected ancient literature in English translation to understand the literary context of the set texts.
Understand the social, cultural and historical contexts of the texts, their authors and audiences.
Identify, analyse and evaluate literary techniques, characterisation, argument and meaning using technical terms.
Translate passages of a set text into English.
Write at length, selecting evidence from the set text and translated material.
Study Homer, Odyssey 16 and 22 set passages, with the English sections.
Study Sophocles' Electra set passages, with the rest in English.
Study Aristophanes' Birds, lines 1-259, with the rest in English.
Study Homer, Iliad 6 and 22 set passages, with the English sections.
Study Sophocles' Oedipus Tyrannus set passages, with the rest in English.
Study Aristophanes' Lysistrata, lines 1-242, with the rest in English.
